Ask which wire protocol the gate hardware speaks, which decides how an entry signal becomes an enter call.
Ask how much daily traffic there is, which decides which database table shape activeTickets should become.
Ask what the driver app screen looks like, which decides which display fields the returned ticket carries.
why: 四维提问是系统做什么 / 出错怎么办 / 什么在范围外 / 未来可能变什么；最后一维决定现在就要留哪些字段和扩展点。
why_en: The four axes are what the system does, what happens on errors, what is out of scope, and what might change later — and that last one decides which fields you leave room for now.
tradeoff: 为未来变化预留扩展点 vs 只按当前需求最小实现
whenOtherWins: 面试官已明说「别考虑未来变化，先做这一版」时，继续追问未来只会占掉实现时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: Ticket 上记录的车辆分类枚举，基础计费用不到，但按车型定价时要靠它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: vehicleType is the vehicle category stored on the ticket; base pricing ignores it, but per-type pricing needs it.

optionExplanations: 未来变化维度直接落到字段上：留了 vehicleType，分车型定价就不用改 Ticket。
闸口硬件已被划出范围，问它不会改变任何类的状态或方法。
本题是单机内存对象设计，没有到选表结构那一层。
UI 同样在范围外，票据字段由计费和验证需求决定，不由界面决定。
optionExplanations_en: The future-change axis lands straight on a field: keep vehicleType and per-type pricing needs no Ticket change.
Gate hardware is explicitly out of scope, so it changes no class state or method here.
This is an in-memory object design; choosing a table shape is a layer this problem never reaches.
UI is out of scope too; ticket fields follow from billing and validation, not from a screen.

scenario: 你已问过满位怎么办、无效票怎么办、丢票怎么办，面试官答「丢票先不考虑，保持简单」。白板上还剩大约三十分钟要写类设计和实现。
scenario_en: You have asked about a full lot, an invalid ticket, and a lost ticket, and the interviewer said to keep it simple and skip lost tickets. About thirty minutes remain for class design and implementation.
q: 接下来继续追问边界情况的正确尺度是什么？
q_en: How far should you keep pushing on edge cases from here?
options: 停下并收敛到需求清单，进入实体设计；已问到的失败模式足够体现思考
继续把二十个边界情况都列到白板上，覆盖得越全越能体现工程严谨性
既然丢票被划出范围，满位和无效票也不必处理，直接实现快乐路径就行
给每个想到的边界情况都先预留一个异常类型，把异常体系建好再写主流程
options_en: Stop, converge on the requirements list, and move into entities; the failure modes you raised already show the thinking.
Keep listing all twenty edge cases on the whiteboard, since broader coverage shows more engineering rigor.
Since lost tickets are out of scope, drop full-lot and invalid-ticket handling too and just build the happy path.
Reserve an exception type for every edge case you can think of and build the exception hierarchy before the main flow.
why: 主动问失败模式是成熟信号，但收益递减；「保持简单」就是收敛信号，代价是主动放弃一部分边界覆盖度。
why_en: Asking about failure modes is a maturity signal, but it has diminishing returns, and keep it simple is your cue to converge and deliberately give up some coverage.
tradeoff: 边界情况覆盖度 vs 有限的白板时间
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说想看你穷举错误路径（比如健壮性专题），那就该继续往下展开。

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统偏离正常路径的具体方式，如满位入场、票据无效、重复出场。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A failure mode is a concrete way the system leaves its normal path, such as entering a full lot or reusing a ticket.

optionExplanations: 三个失败模式已经建立了信号，再问下去挤压的是实现时间。
二十个边界情况会淹没主设计，面试官看到的是不会取舍。
满位和无效票是需求里写死要拒绝的，属于必须实现的部分。
异常体系是为未知变化做的抽象，当前需求只需要两种错误。
optionExplanations_en: Three failure modes already send the signal; more of them only eats into implementation time.
Twenty edge cases bury the main design, and what the interviewer sees is an inability to prioritize.
Full lot and invalid ticket are written into the requirements as rejections, so they must be implemented.
An exception hierarchy is abstraction for unknown change, while the current spec needs only two errors.

scenario: 需求已定稿，你要给 ParkingLot、ParkingSpot、Ticket 三个类各自定出字段和接口，但不知道该从哪个角度切入。
scenario_en: Requirements are locked and you must define fields and methods for ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket, but you are unsure where to start.
q: 对每个类都应该固定问哪两个问题？
q_en: Which two questions should you ask of every class?
options: 它要记住什么才能强制需求，以及它需要支持哪些对外操作
它会被哪些设计模式套用，以及它应该继承哪个基类来复用代码
它在数据库里对应哪张表，以及它的主键和索引要怎么建才够快
它大概有多少行代码，以及它的方法数是否落在单一职责的经验区间内
options_en: What it must remember to enforce the requirements, and which operations it needs to support.
Which design patterns it will fit into, and which base class it should extend to reuse code.
Which database table it maps to, and how its primary key and indexes should be built for speed.
Roughly how many lines it will be, and whether its method count lands in the usual single-responsibility range.
why: state 从需求逐条倒推，methods 从外部真正要发起的动作倒推；两问问完 ParkingLot 就只剩 enter 和 exit 两个公开方法。
why_en: You derive state by walking the requirements one by one and methods from what the outside world actually needs to call, which is how ParkingLot ends up with just enter and exit.
tradeoff: 从需求倒推接口 vs 先套设计模式再找用途
whenOtherWins: 已经有强制的框架契约（必须实现某个接口）时，先看契约再补 state 更省时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类为了强制需求必须长期记住的字段集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is the set of fields a class must remember over time in order to enforce its requirements.

optionExplanations: 需求→必须记住的字段，外部动作→方法，两条线推完接口就闭合了。
先想模式容易做出没有需求支撑的抽象，本题的 Strategy 就是这样被否掉的。
本题是内存对象建模，持久化不在范围内，这两问推不出字段。
行数和方法数是结果不是依据，按它们裁类会切错边界。
optionExplanations_en: Requirements give you the fields and outside actions give you the methods, which closes the interface.
Leading with patterns produces abstractions nothing asked for, which is exactly why Strategy was cut here.
This is in-memory modelling with persistence out of scope, so those questions derive no fields.
Line and method counts are outputs, not inputs; slicing classes by them cuts the wrong boundaries.

scenario: 你在白板上把需求逐条映射成 ParkingLot 必须追踪的字段，已经推出 spots 和 occupiedSpotIds 两项。
scenario_en: On the whiteboard you are mapping each requirement to a field ParkingLot must track, and you already have spots and occupiedSpotIds.
q: 「出场时要验证票据有效」这条需求推出哪个字段？
q_en: Which field does the requirement that exit validates the ticket derive?
options: activeTickets：入场写入、出场删除，查不到就是无效或已用过
usedTicketIds：只记录已经出过场的票，用它反查一张票是否还有效
ticketCounter：一个自增计数器，用序号区间判断票据是否属于本停车场
entryLog：把每次入场追加成不可变日志，验证时扫描日志推出当前状态
options_en: activeTickets: written on entry, deleted on exit, so a miss means invalid or already used.
usedTicketIds: record only tickets that have already exited and check validity against that.
ticketCounter: an incrementing counter, using id ranges to tell whether a ticket belongs to this lot.
entryLog: append every entry as an immutable log and scan it to derive current state at validation.
why: 验证要能立刻回答「这张票现在是否在场」，只有活跃票据表能同时支撑验证、取 entryTime 计费和防重复出场三件事。
why_en: Validation has to answer instantly whether this ticket is still inside, and only the active-ticket map serves validation, the entry time for billing, and double-exit prevention at once.
tradeoff: 维护活跃集合 vs 从历史日志推导当前状态
whenOtherWins: 若要求把「票不存在」和「票已用过」分成两种错误返回，就得额外再存一份已用票集合。

termDefinitions.meaning: Ticket 上记录的入场时间戳，出场时用它减出停车时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: entryTime is the entry timestamp stored on the ticket, subtracted at exit to get the parked duration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一张票被使用两次出场，正确设计应在第二次直接报错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A double exit is the same ticket being used to leave twice, which a correct design rejects the second time.

optionExplanations: 删除票据这一个动作同时完成了释放车位和作废票据两件事。
只存已用票就无法证明一张没见过的票曾经合法入场。
序号区间只能判断票像不像本场发的，判断不了它此刻是否有效。
日志可以复原状态，但每次出场都要扫全量，也没解决重复出场判定。
optionExplanations_en: Deleting the ticket does two jobs at once: it frees the spot and voids the ticket.
Storing only used tickets cannot prove that an unseen ticket was ever legitimately issued.
An id range tells you a ticket looks like ours, not whether it is valid right now.
A log can rebuild state, but every exit rescans everything and double exits still need extra work.

scenario: 有人提议把 hourlyRateCents 从 ParkingLot 拿掉，改成 exit(ticketId, hourlyRateCents)，让调用方每次出场都传入费率。
scenario_en: Someone proposes removing hourlyRateCents from ParkingLot and changing the signature to exit(ticketId, hourlyRateCents) so the caller passes the rate on every exit.
q: 这个改动的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with that change?
options: 调用方被迫知道定价规则，封装被打破，同一个场还可能传出不同费率
多传一个 long 参数会显著抬高 exit 的调用开销，出场路径的延迟变得不可接受
费率一旦作为参数就没法再用整数分来表示，只能退回浮点数，从而引入精度误差
参数化之后 ParkingLot 就不能再实例化多个对象，多停车场的场景反而无法支持
options_en: The caller is forced to know the pricing rule, encapsulation breaks, and one lot can be charged inconsistently.
Passing one extra long noticeably raises the cost of calling exit, making the exit path latency unacceptable.
Once the rate is a parameter it can no longer be integer cents and must fall back to floats, adding rounding error.
After parameterizing, ParkingLot can no longer be instantiated more than once, so multiple lots stop working.
why: 定价是停车场级策略：放在 ParkingLot 里既能给不同 lot 实例化不同费率，也不必全局硬编码；代价只是构造函数多一个参数。
why_en: Pricing is a lot-level policy, so keeping it on ParkingLot lets you instantiate different lots at different rates without hardcoding a global, and the only cost is one more constructor argument.
tradeoff: 编排者持有定价策略 vs 调用方每次出场传参
whenOtherWins: 若费率确实由外部系统按次下发（平台动态定价），把它作为参数或注入 PricingStrategy 才是合理的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内部规则藏在类里，只暴露必要接口，调用方不必知道规则细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation keeps internal rules inside the class and exposes only what callers need, so they need not know the rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把计费算法抽成可替换接口的模式，用于需要多种定价模型时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PricingStrategy is a swappable interface for the fee algorithm, used when several pricing models are needed.

optionExplanations: 费率一旦由外部传，两个入口传不同数字就没人能拦住。
一个 long 参数的开销远小于出场时的物理动作，性能不是这里的矛盾。
参数类型仍然可以是 long 分，与放在哪里无关。
实例化能力恰恰是把费率留在 ParkingLot 才获得的好处。
optionExplanations_en: Once the rate comes from outside, nothing stops two entrances from passing different numbers.
One long argument costs far less than the physical exit itself, so performance is not the tension here.
The parameter can still be a long in cents; storage location has nothing to do with the type.
Being able to instantiate several lots is precisely the benefit of keeping the rate on ParkingLot.

scenario: 有人把 hourlyRateCents 存进 Ticket，让 Ticket 自己算费。某辆车还停在场内时，停车场上调了小时费率。
scenario_en: Someone stores hourlyRateCents on Ticket so the ticket computes its own fee. While a car is still parked, the lot raises its hourly rate.
q: 除了违反单一职责，这个设计还引出什么额外状态问题？
q_en: Beyond breaking single responsibility, what extra state problem does this create?
options: 必须决定是否冻结入场费率，Ticket 从不可变记录变成要维护的状态
Ticket 会因此持有 ParkingSpot 的对象引用，违反迪米特法则，让票据能改车位状态
费率变化会让已经发出的 Ticket 的 id 失效，出场时必须重新给车主签发一张新票据
向上取整的计费公式会失效，不足一小时的停车时长将不能再按整整一小时来收费
options_en: You must decide whether to freeze the entry rate, turning Ticket from an immutable record into managed state.
The ticket ends up holding a ParkingSpot reference, breaking the Law of Demeter and letting it mutate the spot.
The rate change invalidates the ids of already-issued tickets, so a fresh ticket must be reissued at exit.
The round-up formula stops working, so a partial hour can no longer be billed as a full hour.
why: 把定价搬进 Ticket 会让它同时是记录和计算器，还得回答「中途涨价按哪个费率」——这是本可以不存在的状态。
why_en: Moving pricing into the ticket makes it both a record and a calculator, and forces you to answer which rate applies after a mid-stay change, which is state you never needed.
tradeoff: 票据自算费用的内聚 vs 保持票据不可变的简单
whenOtherWins: 若业务要求入场即锁定价格并写进凭证（合同价、预付券），那就该把当时费率快照进票据。

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象构造后字段不再改变，读起来永远是发放那一刻的事实。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An immutable object never changes after construction, so it always reads as the fact recorded at creation time.

termDefinitions.term: 迪米特法则 / Law of Demeter
termDefinitions.meaning: 对象只跟直接邻居说话，不要顺着引用链去调别人的内部对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says an object should talk only to its immediate neighbors, not reach through references into others.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一职责原则：一个类只应有一个变化的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 一旦票上有费率，涨价就变成必须回答的语义问题而不是实现细节。
存 spotId 字符串本来就避开了引用问题，跟费率放哪里无关。
票据 id 是身份标识，费率变化不会让身份失效。
取整逻辑只依赖时长，跟费率存在哪个类上完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: The moment a rate sits on the ticket, a price change becomes a semantic question you must answer.
Storing spotId as a string already avoids reference reach-through; that is unrelated to where the rate lives.
The ticket id is an identity, and changing a rate does not invalidate an identity.
Rounding depends only on duration, so it is untouched by which class holds the rate.

scenario: 类设计讲完，白板上还剩大约十分钟，你准备开始写 ParkingLot 的 enter 和 exit。
scenario_en: Class design is done and about ten minutes remain; you are about to write ParkingLot.enter and exit.
q: 动手之前该先和面试官确认什么？
q_en: What should you confirm with the interviewer before writing anything?
options: 要伪代码、可运行代码还是口头讲，如果写代码用哪种语言
是否可以使用 IDE 和自动补全功能，以免手写时出现语法错误
这段代码会不会被留档，作为后续几轮面试的评分依据之一
要不要连同单元测试一起写完，以及测试覆盖率大致要求多少
options_en: Whether they want pseudocode, runnable code, or just a verbal walkthrough, and in which language.
Whether you may use an IDE with autocomplete so you do not make syntax mistakes by hand.
Whether this code will be kept on file and used as a grading input for later interview rounds.
Whether unit tests should be written alongside it, and roughly what coverage they expect.
why: 各家期望不同：有人要特定语言的可运行代码，有人只要伪代码或口述；一句确认就决定这十分钟花在哪个粒度上。
why_en: Expectations vary a lot: some want runnable code in a specific language, others just pseudocode or a verbal pass, and one question decides how you spend those ten minutes.
tradeoff: 可运行代码的可信度 vs 伪代码的覆盖速度
whenOtherWins: 题面里已经指定语言并要求代码能跑时，直接开写，再确认只是浪费时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: 不绑定语言的结构化描述，够表达控制流和状态变化即可。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode is a language-agnostic structured sketch, precise enough to show control flow and state changes.

optionExplanations: 粒度和语言是唯一会改变你这十分钟产出的两个变量。
工具问题不改变要写什么，通常也不是白板轮的关注点。
评分流程与本轮如何作答无关，问了不会改变你的写法。
基础需求没有提测试，主动加会挤掉核心流程的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Granularity and language are the only two variables that change what those ten minutes produce.
Tooling does not change what you write and is rarely the point of a whiteboard round.
How grading works downstream does not change how you should answer this round.
The base requirements never mention tests, and adding them squeezes out the core flows.

scenario: enter 与 exit 的伪代码刚写完，占用记在 occupiedSpotIds，票据记在 activeTickets。还剩几分钟，你想赶在面试官之前自己发现 bug。
scenario_en: You just finished the enter and exit pseudocode, with occupancy in occupiedSpotIds and tickets in activeTickets. A few minutes remain and you want to find bugs before the interviewer does.
q: 该 trace 哪个场景最能暴露状态管理的 bug？
q_en: Which scenario should you trace to expose state-management bugs?
options: 同一张票入场→出场→再出场，看两个集合是否归零、第二次是否报错
连续调用一百次 enter，观察平均耗时是否随 spots 数量呈线性增长趋势
只 trace 一次成功入场，确认返回票据上的四个字段都被正确填满就够了
手算停 2.5 小时应该收 3 小时的钱，验证取整公式没有把方向写反掉
options_en: One ticket entering, exiting, then exiting again — check both sets return to empty and the second exit errors.
Call enter a hundred times in a row and watch whether average latency grows linearly with the spot count.
Trace just one successful entry and confirm all four fields on the returned ticket are filled correctly.
Hand-compute that a 2.5 hour stay bills three hours, verifying the rounding formula is not inverted.
why: 完整会话把 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两处状态的增与删都走了一遍，再出场一次则检验删除是否真的生效。
why_en: A full session exercises both adds and removes on occupiedSpotIds and activeTickets, and the repeat exit proves the removal actually took effect.
tradeoff: 走完整状态闭环 vs 只验证单点公式
whenOtherWins: 如果只够 trace 一件事，而计费取整规则刚刚被改过，那先手算费用更划算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 手工把一个具体场景在设计上逐步走一遍，检查每步状态是否正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace-through is manually walking one concrete scenario through the design step by step, checking state at each point.

optionExplanations: 一次会话就覆盖了加入、删除、以及删除后的拒绝三种状态转移。
这个规模下的耗时差距只有微秒级，测不出设计层面的问题。
只走快乐路径查不出释放遗漏，而遗漏正是最常见的 bug。
取整只是纯函数，验它不涉及任何跨调用的状态。
optionExplanations_en: One session covers three transitions: adding, removing, and rejecting after removal.
At this scale timing differences are microseconds and reveal nothing about the design.
A happy-path-only trace cannot catch a missed release, which is the most common bug here.
Rounding is a pure function, so checking it touches no state that spans calls.

scenario: 你以 Junior 岗位面这道 Parking Lot 题，时间只够写出能跑通的 enter 与 exit，扩展性一节完全没时间讲。
scenario_en: You are interviewing for a junior role on this parking lot problem, with only enough time to get enter and exit working and none left for extensibility.
q: Junior 档评估看重什么，允许你在哪里被提示？
q_en: What does the junior bar measure, and where are hints acceptable?
options: 看入场出场能否跑通并处理满位与无效票；定价放哪里被提示是允许的
看能否主动讲出反规范化取舍与并发方案；实体划分需要被提示是可以接受的
看能否先给出 PricingStrategy 抽象，再顺势展开多层车库的分配策略讨论
看代码是否零 bug 并附带完整单元测试；设计取舍完全不在这一档评估范围内
options_en: Whether entry and exit work and handle a full lot and invalid tickets; a hint on where pricing lives is fine.
Whether you volunteer the denormalization tradeoff and a concurrency plan; needing hints on entities is fine.
Whether you present a PricingStrategy abstraction first and then open up multi-floor allocation strategies.
Whether the code is bug-free with full unit tests; design tradeoffs are outside this bar entirely.
why: Junior 档的门槛是识别出车位、票据、编排者三样并让流程真的跑通；主动的取舍论证属于 Senior 加分项，不是这一档的下限。
why_en: The junior bar is spotting that you need spots, tickets, and an orchestrator, and getting the flow to actually work; volunteering tradeoffs is a senior signal, not the floor here.
tradeoff: 先做出能工作的系统 vs 先讲清设计取舍
whenOtherWins: 面 Senior 档时同样一份能跑的实现就不够了，要主动摆出反规范化、O(1) 查找、枚举分离这些取舍。

termDefinitions.meaning: 统筹整个流程的类，这里是 ParkingLot，唯一对外暴露 enter 和 exit。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The orchestrator is the class that coordinates the whole flow — here ParkingLot, the only public entry point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一份事实冗余存到多处以换取读取方便，代价是要自己维持一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization stores the same fact in more than one place for easier reads, at the cost of keeping copies in sync yourself.

optionExplanations: 两条主流程加两种拒绝就是可工作系统的最小完整形态。
这是把 Senior 的主动论证和 Junior 的被提示项对调了。
基础需求只有一种费率，先抽策略在任何档位都属于过度设计。
零 bug 加测试不是白板轮的标准，取舍讨论也从未被完全排除。
optionExplanations_en: Two main flows plus two rejections is the smallest complete shape of a working system.
This swaps the senior expectation of volunteering tradeoffs with the junior allowance for hints.
The base spec has a single rate, so leading with a strategy abstraction is over-design at any level.
Bug-free code with tests is not the whiteboard bar, and tradeoffs are never fully excluded.

scenario: 3-5 个入口共用一把方法级锁，你要用数字说服面试官粗粒度锁不是瓶颈。
scenario_en: With 3-5 entrances sharing one method-level lock, you need numbers to show the coarse lock isn't a bottleneck.
q: 补全并发容量的余量估算：
q_en: Fill in the concurrency headroom estimate:
text: 每次 enter 耗时 100 毫秒 → 吞吐 1000÷100 = {{10}} 辆/秒；200 个车位每 2 小时周转一轮 → 需求约 200÷7200 ≈ {{0.03}} 辆/秒；两者相除得到约 {{300}} 倍余量。
why: 吞吐=1000ms÷100ms/次=10 次/秒（entries per second）；需求=200 spots÷7200 秒≈0.03 辆/秒；10÷0.03≈300 倍。这个数字用来判断方法级锁够不够，不必一开始就上读写锁。
why_en: Throughput is 1000ms / 100ms per entry = 10 entries/sec; demand is 200 spots / 7200 seconds ≈ 0.03 vehicles/sec, giving about 300x headroom — enough to justify a simple method-level lock over a read-write lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统实际吞吐超出真实需求的倍数，数字越大代表越不用担心这条路径先成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Headroom is how many times over actual demand your capacity sits — a bigger number means this path is unlikely to be the first bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内系统能处理的请求数，这里是每秒能完成几次 enter。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is how many requests a system can process per unit time — here, how many enter calls per second.

scenario: 系统选了『不存索引，每次现算 occupancy』的方案，随后要支持多入口并发。
scenario_en: The system picked the derive-on-demand occupancy approach, then needs to support multiple concurrent entrances.
q: 按顺序排列推导方案在并发下失效的过程：
q_en: Put the derive-on-demand approach's concurrency failure in order:
steps: occupancy 不单独存，每次入场都遍历 activeTickets 现算。
新增需求：多个入口要能同时处理车辆。
遍历 tickets 求 occupancy 时，不能有别的线程正在改 activeTickets。
只能把整个 activeTickets map 锁起来，读和写都互斥。
所有入口排队等同一把大锁，比只锁一个 Set 索引的粒度粗得多。
why: 推导方案没有冗余数据，但并发下必须把整张 map 锁起来做读写互斥；省下的存储换来了比维护 Set 索引更差的并发粒度。
why_en: The derive-on-demand approach has no redundant state, but under concurrency it forces a lock on the entire ticket map for both reads and writes — trading storage savings for worse concurrency granularity than a maintained Set index.
tradeoff: 无冗余、逻辑最干净 vs 并发时锁粒度粗、吞吐更差

termDefinitions.meaning: 一把锁保护的数据范围大小；锁的范围越大，能并行执行的操作就越少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock granularity is how much data one lock protects — the bigger the scope, the less can run in parallel.

scenario: 3 个车位的场，B 位被 CAR 占用 2.5 小时后正常出场，随后用同一张票再出场一次。
scenario_en: In a 3-spot lot, spot B is claimed by a car for 2.5 hours then exits normally, and the same ticket is used to exit a second time.
q: 按顺序排列这次会话从入场到二次出场的状态变化：
q_en: Put this session's states in order, from entry through the second exit attempt:
steps: 初始：occupiedSpotIds={}，activeTickets={}。
enter(CAR) 找到 spot B → occupiedSpotIds={"B"}，activeTickets 存入 T123。
2.5 小时后 exit("T123")：向上取整按 3 小时收 1500 分，两个索引清空。
再次 exit("T123")：activeTickets 查不到 T123，抛出 invalid ticket 错误，状态不变。
why: 正常入场占位发票、出场按取整计费并清空两个索引，再出场时查不到票直接报错且不改状态——这条 trace 同时验证了计费公式和防重复出场。
why_en: Normal entry claims a spot and issues a ticket, exit bills with round-up and clears both indexes, and a second exit finds nothing and errors without touching state — this trace verifies both the fee formula and double-exit prevention in one pass.
tradeoff: 手动 trace 一次完整场景 vs 等面试官找到 bug 才修

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写完流程后手动带入一组具体数值，逐步核对状态是否符合预期，抢在面试官之前自己发现 bug。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trace-through is manually walking a concrete scenario through your pseudocode step by step to catch bugs before your interviewer does.

scenario: 扩展成多层车库后，你要用『两问法』给新增的 ParkingFloor 类定出状态和方法。
scenario_en: After extending to a multi-floor garage, you apply the two-question method to design the new ParkingFloor class.
q: ParkingFloor 应该记住什么、暴露哪些方法？
q_en: What should ParkingFloor remember, and what methods should it expose?
options: floorNumber 和本层 spots；暴露 findAvailableSpot 和 getAvailableSpotCount 两个方法
只存 floorNumber，本层车位仍留在 ParkingLot 里统一遍历，Floor 不持有 spots
存本层已入场的 Ticket 列表，出场校验也交给 ParkingFloor 处理
只暴露 getAvailableSpotCount，不提供 findAvailableSpot，具体车位靠 ParkingLot 直接读 spots
why: 两问法用在 ParkingFloor 上：要记住 floorNumber 和本层 spots，要支持按类型找空位和统计可用数量，这样 ParkingLot 才能委托给每层而不必直接摸 spots 内部列表。
why_en: Applying the two-question method to ParkingFloor: it should remember its floorNumber and spots, and expose finding a spot by type plus counting availability, so ParkingLot can delegate instead of reaching into each floor's internal list.
tradeoff: Floor 自持 spots 并暴露查找方法 vs ParkingLot 继续统一遍历所有楼层的车位
whenOtherWins: 如果楼层数量很少（比如只有 2 层）且不需要按楼层统计，直接让 ParkingLot 扁平遍历所有 spots 也够用，不必新增 Floor 类。
options_en: floorNumber and this floor's spots as state; expose the findAvailableSpot and getAvailableSpotCount methods.
Store only floorNumber; keep spots in ParkingLot and scan them there, so Floor never owns spots.
Store this floor's active tickets and hand exit validation to ParkingFloor too.
Expose only getAvailableSpotCount, no findAvailableSpot, so ParkingLot reads each floor's spots directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个操作的具体执行交给下层对象自己完成，上层只调用接口而不碰内部细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delegation means handing an operation to a subordinate object to actually perform, while the caller only touches its interface.

optionExplanations: 两问法直接得出的形状：状态是楼层号和本层车位，方法是按类型查找和计数，ParkingLot 只需调用接口。
Floor 不持有 spots，找空位还是要靠 ParkingLot 扁平扫描全部车位，引入 Floor 这一层就没有意义。
出场校验属于编排者职责，票据也不该按楼层拆开存，这会让『查一张票』变成要先知道它在哪层。
少了 findAvailableSpot，ParkingLot 拿到计数后还是得自己遍历该层 spots，Floor 没有真正封装查找逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what the two-question method yields: state is floor number and spots, methods are find-by-type and count.
Without owning spots, Floor adds a layer that does nothing — ParkingLot still has to flat-scan every spot itself.
Exit validation belongs to the orchestrator, and splitting tickets by floor turns 'look up one ticket' into a per-floor search.
Without findAvailableSpot, ParkingLot still has to walk that floor's spots itself after getting the count — no real encapsulation.

scenario: 多层扩展后 spotId 变成 "3-A15" 这种带楼层信息的复合格式。
scenario_en: After the multi-floor extension, spotId becomes a composite like "3-A15" that embeds the floor.
q: 为什么 Ticket 类可以完全不加字段？
q_en: Why can the Ticket class stay unchanged with no new field?
options: spotId 隐式带上楼层，exit 仍按 spotId 查找释放，无需改 Ticket
楼层信息其实从不需要保留，多层扩展后旧的单层 spotId 编号方式继续沿用
Ticket 应该新增 floorNumber 字段，否则出场时无法定位车辆所在楼层
spotId 编码楼层后，Ticket 反而必须改成可变对象才能追加这个信息
why: spotId 从 "B" 变成 "3-A15" 就把楼层信息编码进已有字段，exit 查找逻辑不用改；Ticket 保持不可变、字段不增加。
why_en: Once spotId itself becomes "3-A15", floor information rides along in an existing field, so the exit lookup logic is unchanged and Ticket stays immutable with no new field.
tradeoff: 复合 spotId 隐式带楼层 vs Ticket 显式加 Floor 字段
options_en: spotId implicitly carries the floor, and exit still looks up and frees by spotId, so Ticket doesn't need to change.
Floor information is never actually needed, so the old single-floor spotId scheme just keeps being used unchanged.
Ticket should gain a floorNumber field, or exit can't locate which floor the vehicle is on.
Encoding the floor into spotId actually forces Ticket to become mutable to append that information.
optionExplanations: 字符串本身就是新的复合标识符，找车位、释放车位的逻辑照旧按 id 查找，不需要改 Ticket 的字段。
多层结构下 spot 本来就要按楼层区分身份，"B" 这种旧编号在 10 层车库里会撞号，站不住。
这是本设计选择不做的做法：只有需要在收据上直接展示楼层文字、不想解析字符串时才值得加。
spotId 只是构造时确定的一个字符串值，编码楼层信息不需要让 Ticket 本身变成可变对象。
optionExplanations_en: The string is itself the new composite identifier — lookup and release logic still works by id, no Ticket field needed.
In a multi-floor building, spots need floor-qualified identity or the old scheme like "B" collides across floors.
This is the alternative the design didn't take — only worth it if a receipt must show the floor as text without parsing.
spotId is just a string fixed at construction; encoding the floor into it doesn't require Ticket to become mutable.

scenario: 500 个车位分 5 层，高峰期低层排队而高层空着，你换成按可用车位数选楼层。
scenario_en: 500 spots across 5 floors, with lower floors congested and upper floors empty at peak, so you switch to picking the floor with the most availability.
q: 这段均衡分配伪代码比『第一个匹配楼层』多付出什么代价？
q_en: What extra cost does this balanced-allocation pseudocode pay compared to first-match?
codeSample:
findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
    requiredType = mapVehicleTypeToSpotType(vehicleType)
    bestFloor = null
    maxAvailable = 0
    for floor in floors
        available = floor.getAvailableSpotCount(requiredType)
        if available > maxAvailable
            maxAvailable = available
            bestFloor = floor
    if bestFloor == null
        return null
    return bestFloor.findAvailableSpot(requiredType)
options: 每次入场都要扫一遍全部楼层求最大可用数，换来车位分布更均衡，避免单层拥堵
会漏掉某些楼层完全不参与遍历，换来的是入场处理速度更快
只查一次就直接返回第一层，换来的是完全没有均衡效果
把车位统计逻辑搬到了 ParkingSpot 内部，换来的是 Floor 类可以整个删掉
why: 每次入场要遍历所有楼层取最大可用数，比第一个匹配楼层多一轮 O(floors) 扫描；换来的是车流不再堆积在低楼层。
why_en: Every entry now scans all floors to find the maximum availability, an extra O(floors) pass compared to first-match — the payoff is traffic no longer piles up on the lower floors.
tradeoff: 先匹配即返回，最快但可能堵低楼层 vs 全楼层扫描选最优，稍慢但分布均衡
whenOtherWins: 楼层很少或车流本就稀疏时，第一个匹配楼层的简单遍历已经够用，不值得为均衡多付这轮扫描。
options_en: It scans every floor each entry to find the max availability, trading extra work for a more even spot distribution.
It skips some floors from the scan entirely, trading correctness for faster entry processing.
It checks once and returns the first floor, trading away any real balancing effect.
It moves spot counting into ParkingSpot itself, letting the Floor class be deleted entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算法开销随楼层数量线性增长；这里指每次入场都要遍历一遍全部楼层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(floors) means the cost grows linearly with the number of floors — here, every entry walks the full floor list.

optionExplanations: 代码里 for floor in floors 遍历了全部楼层再挑 maxAvailable，这一轮全量扫描就是换取均衡的代价。
代码没有跳过任何楼层，for 循环覆盖 floors 里的每一个元素，不存在漏扫描的情况。
代码明确记录 maxAvailable 并持续更新 bestFloor，不是找到第一个非空楼层就直接返回。
getAvailableSpotCount 仍在 ParkingFloor 上，代码没挪到 ParkingSpot，也没删 Floor 类。
optionExplanations_en: The for-loop walks every floor to track maxAvailable — that full scan is exactly the cost paid for balance.
The loop doesn't skip any floor; it iterates the whole floors list, so nothing is left out.
The code keeps updating maxAvailable and bestFloor, so it isn't just returning the first non-empty floor.
getAvailableSpotCount stays a ParkingFloor method here — the code neither moves it nor removes the Floor class.

scenario: 写 findAvailableSpot 时你想加一条『优先分配靠近入口的车位』的规则，但需求里没提过。
scenario_en: While writing findAvailableSpot, you're tempted to add a rule preferring spots near the entrance, even though requirements never mentioned it.
q: 这种情况下该怎么处理这条额外规则？
q_en: What should you do with this extra allocation rule?
options: 不主动实现，除非面试官提出或你先问一句是否需要
直接实现，展示的分配逻辑越复杂越能体现工程能力
把它写进 ParkingSpot 的构造函数参数里，默认对所有车位生效
跳过 findAvailableSpot 的实现，先把这条规则的设计文档写清楚
why: 需求没提的分配策略先不做，这是在往未被要求的地方烧时间；真要展示可以先问面试官是否要延伸讨论。
why_en: Don't build allocation logic nobody asked for — that burns time on unrequested features; if you want to show it, ask the interviewer whether they want that extension.
tradeoff: 先写需求内的简单线性扫描 vs 主动加需求外的分配优化
whenOtherWins: 面试官在扩展性环节主动问『如何做更聪明的分配』时，这才是展开 Strategy 模式或就近分配的时机。
options_en: Don't build it proactively — wait for the interviewer to ask, or ask them first whether it's needed.
Implement it right away; the more sophisticated the allocation logic looks, the more it signals skill.
Bake it into ParkingSpot's constructor arguments so it applies to every spot by default.
Skip implementing findAvailableSpot and write up the design for this rule first instead.
optionExplanations: 基础版只需匹配类型并按 O(n) 扫描找到第一个空位，额外偏好逻辑要等被要求才加。
复杂度不等于工程能力，未被要求的功能是在燃烧白板时间，反而显得没有把握好范围。
偏好逻辑是分配策略问题，不是车位固有属性，塞进 ParkingSpot 构造函数混淆了状态归属。
跳过核心方法的实现去写没被要求的文档，本末倒置，交付不出能跑的系统。
optionExplanations_en: The base version only needs to match type and scan for the first free spot; extra preference logic waits until asked.
Complexity isn't skill — building unrequested features burns whiteboard time and signals poor scoping.
Preference is an allocation-policy concern, not an intrinsic spot property; stuffing it into the constructor mixes up which class should hold that state.
Skipping the core method to document an unrequested rule is backwards — you'd have nothing working to show.

scenario: findAvailableSpot 在 enter 中找不到任何兼容空位。
scenario_en: findAvailableSpot finds no compatible free spot inside enter.
q: 此时 enter 应该先做什么？
q_en: What should enter do at this point?
options: 直接返回错误，不改动 occupiedSpotIds 或 activeTickets
先生成一张没有 spotId 的 ticket 占位，等真正有空位时再补上
把某个已经被别人占用的 spot 强制标记为空闲，让这次入场也侥幸成功
先把 occupiedSpotIds 加上一个占位 ID 记录，之后再决定要不要报错
why: 找不到空位就必须在改变任何状态之前返回错误，这样失败路径不会留下半成品的 ticket 或占用记录。
why_en: When no spot is found, enter must return the error before touching any state, so the failure path never leaves a half-written ticket or occupancy record.
tradeoff: 失败路径零副作用 vs 先分配再回滚更复杂但看似更灵活
whenOtherWins: 如果系统未来要支持排队等位，才需要在没有空位时也创建某种『等待中』记录，那已经不是这道题的基础需求。
options_en: Return the error immediately without touching occupiedSpotIds or activeTickets.
Issue a ticket with no spotId as a placeholder and fill it in once a spot opens up.
Force-mark some other vehicle's already-occupied spot as free so this entry can luck into succeeding.
Add a placeholder ID record to occupiedSpotIds first, then decide afterward whether to error.
optionExplanations: 两个索引在失败路径上完全不动，保证下一次入场看到的状态和这次失败前一致。
半成品 ticket 会让 activeTickets 里出现一张指不到真实车位的记录，出场时无法正确释放。
抢占别人车位是更严重的错误，会让原本合法占用的那辆车凭空丢失车位。
占位 ID 会让 occupiedSpotIds 出现一个不对应任何真实 spot 的假条目，污染后续的空位统计。
optionExplanations_en: Neither index moves on the failure path, so the next entry sees exactly the state it would have seen before this attempt.
A half-written ticket leaves an entry in activeTickets pointing at no real spot, so exit can never free it correctly.
Stealing another vehicle's spot is a worse bug — the car that legitimately holds it now has no spot at all.
A placeholder ID pollutes occupiedSpotIds with an entry that maps to no real spot, corrupting later availability checks.
